newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian paedophile victims "could have been saved".
newsitem.headline: Belgian paedophile victims "could have been saved".

text.p: The lives of four Belgian girls who died in the hands of a paedophile ring could have been saved if police investigations had been more efficient, the chairman of a parliamentary commission said on Monday.

"It is not a question, but nearly a certainty that (the girls) could still have been alive...I wonder whether (the investigators) were incompetent, unwilling or were they prevented from doing their job," Marc Verwilghen told the Belgian daily Het Niewsblad.
The all-party commission he chairs resumes hearings on the investigation on Monday after a two-week break.
Late last year Belgium was shocked by the commission hearings, in which police and court investigators often gave conflicting statements about the way the probe had been handled.

Asked by the paper whether a better investigation could have pointed earlier to Marc Dutroux -- the chief suspect in the paedophile kidnap, sex abuse and murder ring -- Verwilghen said: "I am convinced of that."
